decisions.choice: the Ammonite woman, the Moabite woman: mothers from foreign nations
decisions.reason: Ammon and Moab were neighbors east of the Jordan and often enemies of Judah (20:1). Naming the killers' mothers this way may hint that the king who turned to foreign gods was brought down by men of foreign mothers, but the text only gives the facts.

decisions.choice: whose mother was
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the women named are the men's mothers.

decisions.choice: "Zabad", "Simeat", "Jehozabad", "Simrit"
decisions.reason: The usual Spanish forms, matching Spanish 2 Kings 12:22 where the names are the same (Simeat, Jehozabad); Chronicles' other names as the Hebrew has them (m1).

decisions.choice: "Zabad", "Shiméath l'Ammonite", "Yehozabad", "Shimrith la Moabite"
decisions.reason: "Shiméath" and "Yehozabad" as in French 2 Kings 12:22; the French article and feminine ending show that the Ammonite and the Moabite are the mothers.

decisions.choice: "사바드" and "여호사바드"
decisions.reason: The forms follow the 2 Kings 12:22 draft (요사바드, 여호사바드), kept apart from King Jehoshaphat (여호사밧); Zabad is the short form of Jozabad (m1).

decisions.choice: Zabade; Simeate; Jeozabade; Sinrite
decisions.reason: "Simeate" and "Jeozabade" as 2 Kings 12:22 has them in Portuguese; "Zabade" is the short form of Kings' "Jozabade" (m1), written the same way, and "Sinrite" follows "Sinri" of 1 Chronicles 11:45 in Portuguese, with the final "-e" after a consonant.

records.literal_gloss: And his sons, and [the] greatness of the oracle against him, and [the] founding of [the] house of God, look, they [are] written on [the] midrash of [the] book of the kings; and reigned Amaziah his son in his place.

en.L: And his sons, and the many oracles against him, and the founding of the house of God, look, they [are] written in the midrash of the book of the kings. And Amaziah his son reigned in his place.
en.B: The account of his sons, the many oracles against him, and the rebuilding of the house of God are written in the commentary on the Book of the Kings. And his son Amaziah became king in his place.
en.R: What happened to his sons, the many prophecies spoken against him, and how he rebuilt God's temple are all written in the commentary on the book of the kings. His son Amaziah became king after him.

es.L: Y sus hijos, y la abundancia de oráculos contra él, y la fundación de la casa de Dios, he aquí [están] escritos en el midrás del libro de los reyes. Y reinó en su lugar Amasías su hijo.
es.B: Lo referente a sus hijos, los muchos oráculos contra él y la restauración de la casa de Dios están escritos en el comentario del libro de los Reyes. Su hijo Amasías reinó en su lugar.
es.R: Lo que pasó con sus hijos, las muchas profecías que se dijeron contra él y cómo reconstruyó el templo de Dios están escritos en el comentario del libro de los reyes. Su hijo Amasías lo sucedió como rey.

fr.L: Et ses fils, et la multitude des oracles contre lui, et la fondation de la maison de Dieu, voici, ils [sont] écrits dans le midrash du livre des rois. Et Amatsia son fils régna à sa place.
fr.B: Ce qui concerne ses fils, les nombreux oracles prononcés contre lui et la reconstruction de la maison de Dieu est écrit dans le commentaire du livre des Rois. Et Amatsia son fils régna à sa place.
fr.R: Ce qui est arrivé à ses fils, les nombreuses prophéties contre lui et la manière dont il a reconstruit le temple de Dieu, tout cela est écrit dans le commentaire du livre des rois. Son fils Amatsia est devenu roi à sa place.

sw.L: Na wanawe, na wingi wa maneno ya unabii juu yake, na kuwekwa msingi kwa nyumba ya Mungu, tazama, yameandikwa katika midrashi ya kitabu cha wafalme. Na Amazia mwanawe akatawala mahali pake.
sw.B: Habari za wanawe, maneno mengi ya unabii dhidi yake, na kujengwa upya kwa nyumba ya Mungu yameandikwa katika Ufafanuzi wa Kitabu cha Wafalme. Na mwanawe Amazia akawa mfalme mahali pake.
sw.R: Yaliyowapata wanawe, unabii mwingi uliotolewa dhidi yake, na jinsi alivyolijenga upya hekalu la Mungu, yote yameandikwa katika ufafanuzi wa kitabu cha wafalme. Na mwanawe Amazia akawa mfalme mahali pake.

vi.L: Còn về các con trai vua, nhiều lời sấm nghịch cùng vua, và việc xây dựng lại nhà Đức Chúa Trời, kìa, đã được chép trong sách chú giải của sách các vua. A-ma-xia con trai vua trị vì thay vua.
vi.B: Chuyện về các con trai vua, nhiều lời sấm nghịch cùng vua, và việc xây dựng lại nhà Đức Chúa Trời đều được chép trong sách Chú Giải Sách Các Vua. A-ma-xia con trai vua lên kế vị.
vi.R: Những điều xảy ra cho các con trai vua, nhiều lời tiên tri nghịch cùng vua, và việc vua xây lại đền thờ Đức Chúa Trời đều được chép trong sách chú giải về sách các vua. A-ma-xia con trai vua lên kế vị.

ko.L: 그리고 그의 아들들과 그에게 [내린] 많은 경고와 하나님의 집의 기초를 놓은 일은, 보아라, 왕들의 책의 미드라시에 기록되어 있다. 그리고 그의 아들 아마샤가 그를 대신하여 왕이 되었다.
ko.B: 그의 아들들의 이야기와 그에게 내린 많은 경고와 하나님의 집을 다시 세운 일은 왕들의 책 주석에 기록되어 있다. 그의 아들 아마샤가 뒤를 이어 왕이 되었다.
ko.R: 그의 아들들에게 일어난 일과 그를 꾸짖은 많은 예언과 그가 하나님의 성전을 다시 세운 일은 모두 왕들의 책 주석에 기록되어 있다. 그의 아들 아마샤가 뒤를 이어 왕이 되었다.

pt.L: E os seus filhos, e os muitos oráculos contra ele, e a fundação da casa de Deus, eis que estão escritos no midrash do livro dos reis. E Amazias, seu filho, reinou em seu lugar.
pt.B: A história dos seus filhos, os muitos oráculos contra ele e a reconstrução da casa de Deus estão escritos no comentário do Livro dos Reis. E o seu filho Amazias reinou em seu lugar.
pt.R: O que aconteceu com os seus filhos, as muitas profecias contra ele e como ele reconstruiu o templo de Deus estão todos escritos no comentário do livro dos reis. O seu filho Amazias se tornou rei depois dele.

decisions.choice: the midrash of the book of the kings: a written study or account of the kings
alternatives: the story of the book of the kings
the annotations on the book of the kings
decisions.reason: As at 13:22, the only other use of the word: a written work that searched out or set out the history, here of the kings, perhaps a commentary on an older record. It need not mean the later Jewish writings that carry the same name. The work has not survived.

decisions.choice: the many oracles against him
alternatives: the great tribute laid on him
decisions.reason: The word can mean an oracle, a message from God (as in verses 19-20), or a burden laid on someone, such as a tax or tribute. Read the first way, the record tells of the many prophecies against Joash; read the second, of the heavy tribute laid on him (compare 2 Kings 12:19). The Hebrew of the phrase is also unsettled between the written and the read forms.

decisions.choice: the founding of the house of God: its restoration
decisions.reason: "Founding" here means the work of building up again, the repairs of verses 4-14.

decisions.choice: look, they are written: a statement, not a question
decisions.reason: Here Chronicles does not use the question "are they not written?" but says directly that these things are written.

decisions.choice: midrash (Literal); the commentary on the Book of the Kings (Balanced); the commentary on the book of the kings (Readable)
decisions.reason: Worded as at 13:22: Literal keeps the Hebrew word, Balanced and Readable say "commentary". The book it comments on is written as a title at Balanced, as with the other source books of Chronicles (16:11), and plainly at Readable.

decisions.choice: Amaziah his son reigned in his place; became king in his place; became king after him
decisions.reason: Worded as at 2 Kings 12:22.

decisions.choice: "el midrás" (L); "el comentario del libro de los Reyes" (B); "el comentario del libro de los reyes" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew word in its Spanish spelling; Balanced and Readable say "comentario", as the English does (m1). The successor formula as the terms note.

decisions.choice: "le midrash" (Literal); "le commentaire du livre des Rois" (Balanced); "le commentaire du livre des rois" (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew word (m1); Balanced writes the book's name as a title.

decisions.choice: midrashi (L); Ufafanuzi wa Kitabu cha Wafalme (B); ufafanuzi wa kitabu cha wafalme (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew word, as the English does; Balanced and Readable say "ufafanuzi" (commentary).

decisions.choice: "sách chú giải của sách các vua" (L); "sách Chú Giải Sách Các Vua" (B); "sách chú giải về sách các vua" (R)
decisions.reason: The *midrash* was a written study or account (m1); Vietnamese gives its sense at every level rather than a transliteration readers would not know.

decisions.choice: "A-ma-xia con trai vua trị vì thay vua" (L); "A-ma-xia con trai vua lên kế vị" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's successor formula, as the Kings drafts.

decisions.choice: "왕들의 책의 미드라시" (Literal); "왕들의 책 주석" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew word, as the English does; Balanced and Readable say "commentary" (m1). "많은 경고" renders "the greatness of the oracle", the reading the English takes (m2).

decisions.choice: o midrash (L), o comentário (B, R); o Livro dos Reis (B); Amazias, seu filho, reinou em seu lugar (L)
decisions.reason: The source keeps the words 13:22 gives it in Portuguese, "midrash" at Literal and "comentário" at Balanced and Readable (m1), with the book as a title at Balanced, as the English has it. Chronicles states that these things are written, without the question of Kings (m4). The succession keeps the words of 2 Kings 12:22 in Portuguese at each level.
